summary: Benton County, OR summit lookout; register dates its L-4 tower to 1939; newspapers show a summit lookout in 1937, a station being erected in December 1938, road work in 1939 and new towers in use in July 1941; removed or destroyed 1950; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: L-4 tower per the register; a 1940 newspaper describes a new station atop a 10-foot tower with storage space beneath
facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in 1950 (sources differ on which); no source describes the site today

staffing.status: lookouts housed in tents in 1940, then in new towers from 1941

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Siuslaw National Forest); Polk-Benton District of the State Board of Forestry was to occupy and maintain the station from 1946 under an agreement

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register and firelookout.com date the L-4 tower to 1939. Newspapers show a lookout on the summit in August 1937, a new station being erected on December 8, 1938, road work from September 10, 1939, and a new tower in use in July 1941. The story gives both.
Register says removed in 1950; firelookout.com says destroyed in 1950; the Forest Lookouts page gives no date and says removed.

notes_for_editor: Brief coordinates conflict (FFLOS 44.46235, -123.50021 vs West US lookouts 44.46679, -123.50371); not used in the story. Height 3.0 m comes from the 1940 newspaper's 10-foot tower; the register gives no height, so treat it as approximate. The FFLOS registration date in the brief (Sept 22, 2010) did not appear in the fetched text, so there is no fflos_registered event. The 1946 item is a plan ('will occupy and maintain'), not a confirmed occupation. No source describes the site today; the Alsea Historical Society Facebook post was not readable.
